bull.b: Revenue and earnings are recovering at scale, while raised 2026 targets point to continued expansion rather than a single-quarter rebound. Higher EBITDA and EPS should improve internal funding capacity and reinforce MasTec’s ability to pursue infrastructure demand.

Record backlog and book-to-bill above one indicate demand exceeds current execution, improving medium-term revenue visibility. Growth across clean energy, power delivery, and pipeline reduces reliance on one end-market and supports a broader infrastructure platform.

Superior adds mission-critical and data-center electrical capabilities, roughly 3,000 employees, and a meaningful expected revenue and EBITDA contribution. The broader offering can deepen cross-selling and geographic reach while strengthening MasTec’s position in complex infrastructure work.

bear.b: Despite improvement, TTM EBIT and EBITDA margins remain modest and below 2021 levels. This thin-margin profile leaves less room for project execution issues or cost pressure and makes sustained profitability dependent on disciplined delivery and favorable business mix.

Free cash flow is positive but converts only about 45% of reported net income and has declined modestly. Working-capital investment and project timing can delay cash realization, limiting the reliability of earnings as a source of internally funded growth.

The Superior transaction increases pro forma leverage and leaves management reliant on future cash generation to reduce it. Higher debt can limit financial flexibility, making deleveraging, integration, and delivery of the acquisition’s expected earnings important execution priorities.
